tldr: A legacy server on custom GHCR images redeployed in full on every nightly run and never left its old `0 2 * * *` cron. This PR fixes both from inside the normal cron run, with no manual steps.

summary.goal: Let a legacy `/opt/seed` install using custom GHCR images take the cheap **no-change** path and run on the current `*/10` schedule.
summary.change: The image check now compares against `web_image`/`site_image` via `expectedServiceImages`. A new `migrateLegacyCron` rewrites old crons during a headless deploy. A new `resolveBunPath` gives cron an absolute bun path.
summary.why: The server only ever runs `upgrade` + `deploy` from cron, so the fix has to apply itself there. Every migration step backs off rather than leave cron pointing at a missing or stale script.

blocks.title: What one headless cron run does now
blocks.lede: `cmdDeploy` now runs a migration before `deploy()`. Inside `deploy()`, the no-change check reads the configured images.
blocks.tourIntro: Four steps, in the order the server runs them.

steps.title: Cron starts a headless deploy
steps.text: The old line still runs the old script: `0 2 * * *` against `/opt/seed/deploy.js`. `upgrade` has already pulled this PR's `dist/deploy.js` into place, so this `deploy` runs the new code.

steps.title: Migrate the cron first
steps.text: `migrateLegacyCron` runs before `deploy()`, which means before the compose fetch, so a GitHub timeout can't block it. It copies the script to the fixed path, then rewrites cron and the `seed-deploy` wrapper.

steps.title: Absolute bun path
steps.text: Cron's `PATH` has no `/root/.bun/bin`. The old fallback `/usr/local/bin/bun` doesn't exist on this box, so a migration run from cron would have broken cron for good. Both writers now use `resolveBunPath`.

steps.title: Compare against the configured images
steps.text: The no-change check used to expect `seedhypermedia/*:<channel>`, so GHCR containers never matched and every run redeployed. It now asks `expectedServiceImages`, the same fallback the compose file, doctor and rollback use.

blocks.title: Bug 1: the image check ignored `web_image` / `site_image`
blocks.lede: With a fork's web image configured, the hard-coded upstream image names could never match. The fast path was skipped on every run.

notes.text: The old expectation ignored the config overrides. The server logged `Running containers do not match release channel 'main'` and redeployed every night.
Reuses the existing helper: `web_image || seedhypermedia/web:<channel>`. This is the same fallback the compose file uses, so the check and the deployment can't disagree.

blocks.title: Bug 2: when `migrateLegacyCron` touches the crontab, and when it backs off
blocks.lede: `setupCron` only runs from the wizard and `seed-deploy cron`, so old installs never moved. The migration rewrites cron only if every check passes.

items.title: No `# seed-deploy` line → do nothing
items.text: Seed never installed cron on this box, so the migration doesn't create one.

items.title: Line belongs to another node → do nothing
items.text: The line must mention this node's `"<seedDir>/deploy.js"` or `--dir "<seedDir>"`. A manual `--dir <other>` run can't take over the cron.

items.title: Seed lines already current → do nothing
items.text: It compares `extractSeedCronLines` before and after `buildCrontab`, so repeat runs are idempotent.

items.title: Copy the running script to the fixed path
items.text: Only when the target is missing or its sha256 differs. It tries `mkdir -p && cp`, then the same with `sudo`, then `chown` back to the cron user so unattended `upgrade` can replace the file later.

items.title: Copy failed or script missing → warn and leave cron alone
items.text: Cron never points at a missing or stale script. This check came from review findings fixed in `1527c49`.

items.title: Rewrite cron + wrapper, log the move
items.text: `setupCron` + `installWrapper`, then the log line `Migrated legacy cron (0 2 * * * → */10) to /usr/local/lib/seed/deploy.js.`

blocks.title: Why the migration runs inside the headless deploy
blocks.question: How does an unattended legacy server get onto the new cron?
blocks.context: On the unattended server, `upgrade` + `deploy` only run from the old cron.

options.name: Ask the operator to run `seed-deploy cron`
cons: Needs a manual step on every legacy box
The 02:00 schedule stays until someone remembers

options.name: Migrate in `cmdDeploy`, before `deploy()`
options.summary: Self-applying on the next nightly run. Wrapped in try/catch.
pros: Runs before the compose fetch, so a GitHub timeout can't block it
cons: Code that edits the crontab now runs on every headless deploy, so it needs strict guards (previous section)

blocks.why: From the PR description: "Both fixes apply themselves through the normal `upgrade` + `deploy` cron run, with no manual steps." Migrating before `deploy()` means "a GitHub fetch timeout can't block it."

blocks.title: What the server does on its first run after merge

items.title: 02:00: `upgrade` on the old path
items.text: Pulls the new `dist/deploy.js` from `custom-images` into `/opt/seed/deploy.js`. `cmdUpgrade` reads `deploy_url` from the `--dir` config, so it still fetches the fork, not upstream S3.

items.title: `deploy`, now running the new code
items.text: Copies itself to `/usr/local/lib/seed/deploy.js` and rewrites cron to `*/10 … --dir "/opt/seed" upgrade …; … deploy … # seed-deploy`. The 4-hourly `prune -a` becomes the stock hourly `docker image prune -f --filter "until=1h"`, which keeps tagged images.

items.title: Same run: no-change path
items.text: If compose, env and images are unchanged, it skips the redeploy. From then on it runs every 10 minutes from the fixed path.

files.note: 3 image-match cases, bun fallback, 6 `migrateLegacyCron` cases (idempotent, other node, copy failure, sudo + chown)
rebuilt with the pinned Bun 1.3.10 (CI checks it isn't stale)

scenes.say: One legacy Seed server kept redeploying every night and never moved off its old cron. Here's how this PR fixes both, without anyone logging in.
Every night, cron starts a headless deploy.
First, the new *migrateLegacyCron* runs, before deploy and before any network fetch. It copies the script to a fixed path and rewrites cron.
Cron has no bun on its PATH, so both cron writers now resolve an *absolute bun path*.
Then deploy checks whether the running containers match the config. That check now reads the *configured images* instead of assuming Docker Hub.
Before, it expected seedhypermedia images, so GHCR containers *never matched* and every run redeployed.
Now it loops over *expectedServiceImages*, the same fallback the compose file uses.
The migration does nothing when there's no seed cron, when the line belongs to another node, or when it's already current.
If it can't install the script, it *leaves cron alone*, so cron never points at a missing or stale file.
On the first run after merge, the server upgrades, migrates itself to every ten minutes, and takes the no-change path.
